changes.summary: The exhibition aims to present an overview of the body of work produced by Paul Cezanne (1839-1906) in terms of his artistic legacy, in the innovative form of a concise, ongoing dialogue. It bears witness to the artist’s incomparable legacy, from the time when, in seclusion in Aix, some people wondered whether he really existed, to the 20th-century “Cezanne Myth”, as founding father of pictorial modernity. Hence, with a strong historiographical focus, while taking care not to neglect the iconographic side of things, the exhibition takes account of the way that Cezanne – and which Cezanne? – was able to be seen and purchased by artists in the 1880s, a period when he no longer exhibited , thanks to “Père” Tanguy and a few collectors, some of whom were artists themselves. It goes on to cover milestones in the artist’s French and then international recognition, through the first monographic exhibitions organized by Ambroise Vollard between 1895 and 1901, the acceptance of two of his works by Musée du Luxembourg thanks to the Caillebotte bequest (1894), followed by the monographic exhibitions at the Autumn Salon and the first major international exhibitions he was included in. These events ensured the artist’s critical and commercial success and raised him to the rank of father of modernity in the eyes of the European avant-garde movements of the 1910s and the great international collectors alike.
